correctness.rationale: Verified h^{-1}(v)=sqrt(1+3v)-1 and derivative G'_theta=theta(1+z)(1+ct(z))^{-1/2}(1-dt(z))^{-3/2}, t(z)=z²+2z, c=(4theta−1)/3, d=(1−theta)/3. If theta≤1/4 then c≤0 and factors have positive coefficients; if 1/4<theta≤2/5, 0<c≤d, derivative factorizes as (1-dt)^{-1}(1-(d-c)t-cdt²)^{-1/2} and is coefficientwise positive. G(1)=1, radicands nonsingular on unit disc, semigroup via Mobius conjugacy. Denominator positive branch singularity r=sqrt((4−theta)/(1−theta))−1; numerator conjugate singularities modulus rho=sqrt(3/(4theta−1)); crossing unique theta*. Pole r gives positive n^{-1/2} asymptotic, numerator branch zeros give O(n^{-3/2}) at equality. Beyond crossing positive-radius point rho analytic, while radius rho finite; Pringsheim on both eventual signs excludes either, giving infinitely many of each. Independent exact rational coefficients through n=80 for theta=1/10,1/4,2/5,1/2 positive; theta=11/20 first negative index39. Finite tests cannot prove infinite claims.
